content: The pharmacokinetics of nitazoxanide have not been studied in patients with impaired renal or hepatic function. Therefore, nitazoxanide should be used cautiously in individuals with hepatic or biliary disease, renal disease, or a combination of renal and hepatic disease. Both Alinia Tablets and Alinia for Oral Suspension should be taken with food. For diabetic patients and their caregivers, it is important to note that the oral suspension contains 1.48 grams of sucrose per 5 mL. Tizoxanide, the active metabolite of nitazoxanide, is highly bound to plasma proteins (>99.9%). As a result, caution is advised when nitazoxanide is co-administered with other drugs that are also highly protein-bound and have narrow therapeutic indices, such as warfarin, due to the potential for competition at binding sites. In vitro studies indicate that tizoxanide does not significantly inhibit cytochrome P450 enzymes. Although no in vivo drug interaction studies have been conducted, it is anticipated that nitazoxanide is unlikely to interact significantly with drugs metabolized by or inhibiting cytochrome P450 enzymes. Long-term studies to evaluate the carcinogenic potential of nitazoxanide have not been conducted. Genotoxicity testing revealed that nitazoxanide was not genotoxic in the Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cell chromosomal aberration assay or the mouse micronucleus assay. However, it was genotoxic in one bacterial strain (TA 100) during the Ames bacterial mutation assay. Fertility studies in rats showed no adverse effects on male or female fertility at doses of 2,400 mg/kg/day, which is approximately 20 times the clinical adult dose when adjusted for body surface area. Nitazoxanide is classified as Pregnancy Category B. Reproductive studies in rats at doses up to 3,200 mg/kg/day (approximately 26 times the clinical adult dose adjusted for body surface area) and in rabbits at doses up to 100 mg/kg/day (approximately 2 times the clinical adult dose adjusted for body surface area) did not show evidence of impaired fertility or harm to the fetus. However, there are no adequate and well-controlled studies of nitazoxanide use in pregnant women. It is unknown whether nitazoxanide is excreted in human breast milk. Given that many drugs are excreted in breast milk, caution should be exercised when administering nitazoxanide to nursing mothers. A single Alinia Tablet contains more nitazoxanide than is recommended for pediatric patients aged 11 years or younger and should not be used in this population. Instead, Alinia for Oral Suspension should be used for pediatric dosing. The safety and efficacy of Alinia for Oral Suspension have not been established in children under 1 year of age. Clinical studies of Alinia Tablets and Alinia for Oral Suspension did not include enough participants aged 65 years and older to determine whether their response differs from that of younger patients. In elderly patients, the potential for decreased hepatic, renal, or cardiac function, as well as the presence of other diseases or concurrent drug therapies, should be taken into account when prescribing nitazoxanide. As noted earlier, caution is advised when administering this medication to patients with renal or hepatic impairment. The use of Alinia Tablets and Alinia for Oral Suspension has not been studied for the treatment of diarrhea caused by Giardia lamblia in HIV-infected or immunodeficient patients. Additionally, these formulations have not been shown to be more effective than placebo for treating diarrhea caused by Cryptosporidium parvum in HIV-infected or immunodeficient individuals.
